/itineraryStops/1/timeUsed/1.source_en: Memorial Service Hall + 12-min English documentary (~15 min)

/itineraryStops/1/timeUsed/2.source_en: Wall of Remembrance + Memorabilia Hall (~20 min)

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/2.source_en: Return buffer built into the plan

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/3.source_en: Main Gate by Korean architect **Kim Joong-up (1966)**

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/4.source_en: **'Turn Toward Busan' ceremony** Nov 11 at 11:00 AM (synchronized worldwide)

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/6.source_en: **Frank Gaylord US Korean War Monument (2013, dedicated by American Battle Monuments Commission)** — by the same sculptor as the National Mall Korean War Veterans Memorial 'The Column' in Washington DC (1995)

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/7.source_en: **Adjacent UN Sculpture Park** — 34 sculptures donated by sculptors from 21 nations who fought in the Korean War; opened October 24, 2001 as 50th-anniversary commemoration

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/8.source_en: **UN General Assembly Resolution 977(X) of December 15, 1955** officially established UNMCK as UN-administered protected territory under international ⟦G0⟧ Commission

/itineraryStops/1/whyOnRoute.source_en: Private routing is the main advantage of this product: less waiting, more control, and a schedule planned around your cruise time.

/itineraryStops/1/description.source_en: This is a private tour, so the day can be shaped around your interests, pace, weather, and all-aboard time. The guide helps choose a realistic route rather than overloading the day with too many distant stops.

/itineraryStops/2/timeUsed/2.source_en: Walk to Yeongdo Lighthouse + 'Light Beyond Limitation' sculpture (~15 min)

/itineraryStops/2/timeUsed/3.source_en: Cliff-edge views toward Mangbuseok Rock + Sinseon Rock area (~20 min)

/itineraryStops/2/timeUsed/4.source_en: Train back to entrance + reassemble (~10 min)

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/3.source_en: **3-story Observatory** with views to **Tsushima Island (Japan, 50 km)** on clear days

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/4.source_en: **Danubi Train** ~₩4,000 RT — 5 stops along 4.3 km coastal loop

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/5.source_en: **Mangbuseok Rock** legend + **'Light Beyond Limitation' sculpture** (Ji Sul Won Kyung-Lee)

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/6.source_en: Park free; trails strenuous (lighthouse area = many steep stairs)

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/7.source_en: **Designated Busan National Geopark site (2013) + State-Designated Cultural Property Scenic Site No. 17 (2005)** — dual heritage status protecting the Cretaceous-era sedimentary cliffs, wave-cut terraces, orbicular hornfels, and slumping structures

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/8.source_en: **Annual Hydrangea Culture Festival** at Taejongsa Temple (late June – early July) draws 100,000+ visitors to the bigleaf-hydrangea flower carpet inside the park grounds

/itineraryStops/2/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Skip the strenuous 4.3 km hike — board the **Danubi Train** for the 5-stop loop. **Taejongsa Temple's Hydrangea Festival** runs late June to early July. Lighthouse area has many steep stairs — not stroller-friendly.

/itineraryStops/2/whyOnRoute.source_en: The east coast option is scenic and highly recognizable for first-time visitors.

/itineraryStops/2/convenience/parking.source_en: Large free parking lot at the entrance plaza

/itineraryStops/2/convenience/restroom.source_en: At the entrance plaza, Observatory, and Yeongdo Lighthouse area

/itineraryStops/2/description.source_en:
Popular east-side choices include ⟦G0⟧ Temple, Cheongsapo, Haeundae Blue Line Park or Sky Capsule area, Haeundae Beach, and Gwangalli Beach. 

This route is best for guests who want coastal views and Busan’s seaside atmosphere.

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/closed.source_en: Open year-round (Danubi Train suspends in heavy rain or strong wind)

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Full 4.3 km coastal loop is strenuous; **Danubi Train** stops at Pebble Beach → Gumyeongsa → Observatory → Yeongdo Lighthouse → Taejongsa Temple

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/admission.source_en: FREE park entry; **Danubi Train ~₩4,000 round-trip adult**, ~₩2,000 child
